Subject: Re: Discovery — Performance SLOs / next steps

Hi Sara — great call this morning, thanks for walking us through EdgeFin's streaming use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Recap of requirements
- Latency target (p95): <= 120ms for 8k-token context under streaming mode
- Target throughput: 200 reqs/s sustained for inference pipeline (avg tokens per request ~450)
- Concurrency: support 80 concurrent streams with graceful degradation above 100
- Streaming: need server-sent-events with partial token flush and stable ordering semantics
- Output quality: minimal truncation on long-form outputs; ability to pin model family for determinism

Proposed benchmark scope
- Use the prompt set you shared (we'll ask for final CSV) + 3 synthetic streaming traces to simulate user sessions
- Measure: p50/p95/p99 latency (first token and full response), tokens/sec throughput, end-to-end tail latency under concurrency, memory (GPU) per-request, and KV cache hit rates
- Reproducibility: run each scenario 3x across two identical GPU configs, seed prompts where applicable, and record raw traces + env specs

Next steps
1) Can you confirm the final prompt CSV and attach the eval_harness spec you mentioned?
2) We'll share our benchmark harness and a short methodology doc (measurement definitions + exact commands) by EOD tomorrow.
3) Book a 30-min sync early next week to finalize configs before we run the pilot.

Attaching initial SLO matrix (draft) — see edgefin_initial_slo_matrix.xlsx.

Thanks — I'll loop in Stephanie for any operational questions about streaming semantics.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap, that matches our internal notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

Clarifications
- The 120ms p95 is for first-token latency in streaming mode; full-response latency can be higher (~600ms typical for 450-token avg).
- Throughput target 200 reqs/s is peak sustained; we expect diurnal spikes up to 350 for short periods.
- Concurrency 80 is concurrent open SSE streams — each stream can send 1–3 incremental prompts per minute.

Attached are the prompt set (benchmark_prompt_set_v2.csv) and a short eval harness spec (eval_harness_spec.md) that includes example curl commands we used internally. We anonymized customer prompts and added marker tags for streaming traces.

Questions for Redwood
1) For reproducibility, can you share exact GPU instance types and CUDA/cuBLAS versions used in the pilot?
2) What's your approach to measuring first-token vs. full-response latency when streaming is involved? We need consistent definitions to compare across runs.

We'll regroup after you send your harness and schedule the sync.

—Sara
Sara Jensen
Head of Platform
EdgeFin Solutions

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery — Performance SLOs / next steps

Thanks Sara — got the files. Quick answers and attached methodology summary. Highlights below: 

Environment details (pilot baseline)
- GPU: 4x A100-SXM4 40GB (NVIDIA driver 525.85.12, CUDA 11.8, cuBLAS 11.10)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
- Redwood runtime v2.4.1 with continuous-batching and streaming-commit enabled

Measurement definitions
- First-token latency (FTL): time from request arrival at ingress to emission of the first non-empty token on the SSE stream. Measured at ingress and service egress, logged as t_ingress -> t_first_token.
- Full-response latency (FRL): time from request arrival to final EOS token. For streaming runs we also record inter-token delta statistics (median, 95th).
- Throughput: measured as successfully completed responses/sec over 60s windows, reported as sustained and peak.
- Concurrency stress: follow your trace generator for open streams; we will ramp to target concurrency and hold for 10 minutes to measure tail behavior.

Reproducibility notes
- We'll provide the harness container image (sha256) and an env spec file; runs are instrumented with deterministic seeding for synthetic traces.
- Raw traces (request/response + kernel-level metrics) and a summary JSON will be uploaded to the GH results directory for transparency.

Deliverables we'll push to the repo
- methodology.md (measurement definitions + exact CLI commands)
- harness/dockerfile and run scripts (curl + SSE runner)
- sample raw traces and post-processed CSVs for p50/p95/p99 and throughput curves

I'll attach methodology.md and a short runbook. Can Rishi and Marcus weigh in on whether the A100 baseline is sufficient or if we should add an 8x H100 (or q8 quantized) comparison for cost/latency trade-offs?

Proposed next sync: Mon Jun 14 10:00am PT — I'll send a calendar invite after confirmation.

Best,
Marissa

Quick note on reproducibility and measurement rig: 

- Hardware parity matters: we'll mirror your prod-like instance family where possible. If EdgeFin can run one quick baseline on an H100 pool (if available) we can include that as a comparison — otherwise the A100 baseline is fine.
- Seed determinism: we will ensure synthetic traces are seeded; real customer traces may vary so we'll run those as "wildcard" tests and report variance separately.
- Streaming definition: measure FTL at both ingress and service egress to capture network vs. model compute split. We'll also capture per-token emission deltas to detect token stalling issues.
- Quantization/variant policy: we'll run float32, q8_0, and q4f16 variants where model artifacts are supported and include a quality delta check (ROUGE/EM/BLEU depending on task).

I'll join the Monday sync.

-rishi
VP, Applied ML
Redwood Inference
